title: Precision Cost Sprints: hypothesis-driven econ experiments across batching, KV caching, and quant profiles
creator: Asha Patel
description: Run a short, focused set of hypothesis-driven sprints to quantify unit-economics improvements from three levers: request-level batching, prefix/KV caching policies, and per-workload quantization profiles. Deliver concrete config recommendations and a scoring rubric for production rollout decisions.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Completed experiment matrix covering at least 8 representative workloads; 2) Collected token-level latency, p99, and CPU/GPU utilization per cell; 3) Calculated net cost-per-response delta and quality regression score for each variant; 4) Published runbook with recommended default profiles and guardrails; 5) Sign-off from Runtime, Infra, and Product on rollout plan.
tasks: Define 8 workload archetypes and baseline traces (PM + Eng)
Instrument token-level cost and quality signals in Console dashboards (ENG)
Create experiment harness to run batching/cache/quant permutations (ENG)
Run smoke runs and iterate on measurement windows (PM + ENG)
Analyze quality regressions with eval harness and human spot checks (ML/Research)
Draft rollout runbook and canary criteria (PM)
Automate configuration suggestions in Optimize pilot (Product-Example)
progress_updates: 2026-02-20: Kickoff — aligned on goals, success metrics, and eight workload archetypes. Logged sample traces to S3 for baseline generation.
2026-02-25: Eng spike complete — small harness built to replay traces with variable batch sizes and KV cache TTLs. Early results show 12-18% token cost reduction for latency-tolerant qna workloads.
2026-03-02: Added quantization axis — initial 4-bit int8-like quant profiles integrated. Observed mild (2-4%) quality drift on long-context summarization; flagged for human review.
2026-03-08: Dashboard instrumentation merged (PR: github.com/redwood/runtime/pulls/1189). Console shows per-request cost breakdown; p99 pipeline traces in APM linked to experiment cells.

2026-03-12: Mid-sprint review — decided to prioritize batching+cache combos for immediate rollout pilot; quant profiles to remain in experimental channel until further evals complete. Assigned follow-ups to ENG and Research.
review_feedback: Runtime lead (Priya Rao): recommend throttled batching with adaptive windowing to avoid latency cliffs — see design note in Confluence.
Research (Daniel Kim): require a minimum of 500 human evals for any quant profile that yields >8% cost improvement to ensure quality preservation.
Security (Lena Schmidt): KV cache TTLs must not persist user-sensitive prefixes — add checklists to runbook.
Sales engineering: request a short summary artifact to help customers understand trade-offs between latency, cost, and quality.
decisions: Pivot: run batching+cache pilot for Q2 Dedicated customers with opt-in flag; defer global default changes until quant regressions are resolved.
Adopt a scoring rubric combining cost delta, p99 delta, and quality regression to recommend profile tiers (safe / balanced / aggressive).
Require cross-team sign-off for any default change affecting >5% of traffic or with >10% p99 impact.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: batching increases tail latency for small, latency-sensitive routes. Mitigation: adaptive per-route batching limits and emergency fallback to single-request mode.
Risk: quantization introduces subtle quality regressions on long-context prompts. Mitigation: human-in-the-loop evals and canarying to <1% of traffic with rollback triggers.
Risk: KV caching may leak encoded PII if not sanitized. Mitigation: sanitize prefixes and add audit log entries per cache write.
next_steps: Execute 4-week pilot on Dedicated with opt-in customers (ENG to schedule infra)
Complete 1,000 human evals for top quant candidates (Research)
Write Optimize integration stub to surface suggested profiles in Console (Product)
Prepare customer-facing FAQ and decision flow for SEs (PM + GTM)
